what_was_done: junit_runner.build_suite wraps each source-tree load (loader.loadTestsFromName) in try/except Exception — loadTestsFromName catches ImportError alone, so a module dying at import with a SyntaxError or a NameError used to crash the runner and leave no build/junit.xml. On any failure build_suite adds _import_error_case(name, traceback.format_exc()): one error case named <module>::import_error whose body raises ImportError carrying 'Failed to import test module: <module>' plus the original traceback, so the report keeps type=ImportError as discovery gives. Like the discovery case (unittest.loader._FailedTest) it carries no file attribute — the module's own tests are unknown, and a file would class the case out of the red gate's new tests — so RecordingResult._record honours a test's junit_file attribute (falling back to file_of as before) and the case is counted: the gate says 'build or harness error in <module>::import_error: ImportError' and never 'the test command wrote no JUnit report'. The runner module and build_suite docstrings, the sample README sentence and rewrite/spec/packaging/sample-project.md now say the report survives any import failure (spec_lint run). Tests: test_sample_runner.py::test_syntax_broken_source_module_still_writes_the_report and ::test_name_error_at_import_names_the_error (runner level: exit 1, report written with the ImportError case, original SyntaxError/NameError traceback in it, the tests that ran still reported) and ::test_red_survives_source_modules_that_die_at_import (through the real red gate with both a syntax-broken and a NameError tally/test_*.py: 'build or harness error ... ImportError' for each, never 'wrote no JUnit report'). All three verified to fail with the try/except removed.
where: next/tests/e2e/sample-project/tools/junit_runner.py (build_suite, _import_error_case, RecordingResult._record); next/tests/e2e/sample-project/README.md (sentence extended); rewrite/spec/packaging/sample-project.md (paragraph extended); tests: next/tests/unit/test_sample_runner.py

what_was_done: The missing test for build_suite's source-tree function collection (the suite.addTests(_function_cases_of(name)) line in the */test_*.py loop) is in: test_sample_runner.py::test_source_tree_function_reaches_the_report writes tally/test_fn.py holding a failing module-level test_ac1_src_red, runs tools/junit_runner.py, and asserts exit 1, that the case tally.test_fn::test_ac1_src_red is a failure with file_attr 'tally/test_fn.py' and criteria_of(name) == 'AC-1'. Verified to fail (KeyError: the case is absent from the report and the runner exits 0) with only the collection line removed; the unmutated runner reports it as a failure, exactly the behaviour the finding confirmed as right.

function_cases now treats a member for which inspect.iscoroutinefunction, inspect.isasyncgenfunction or inspect.isgeneratorfunction is true like the required-parameter case: _non_synchronous(member) short-circuits the plain wrap, and the function is reported as an error case of type TypeError whose message says '<module>.<name>: the runner runs plain synchronous test functions with no parameters'. Previously such a function was wrapped in _FunctionTestCase, whose call threw the coroutine or generator away: the case passed with the body never run, so the red gate saw a new test that already passes and the green gate accepted a pass where nothing ran. The function_cases docstring and the sample README sentence say the rule for coroutine, async-generator and generator functions. Test: test_sample_runner.py::test_async_and_generator_functions_are_reported_as_errors writes tests/test_async.py with all three kinds (a coroutine, an async generator, a plain generator, each red if run) and asserts each is an error of type TypeError, none passed, and 'plain synchronous test functions' in the report. Verified to fail with the _non_synchronous condition reverted (the cases came back passed).
